data.title: How Ekumen ids are formed
data.question: Ids like D-012 or R1 are opaque to read, and sequential numbers collide when two branches each create "the next" one. What should decision and task ids look like?

options.tradeoff: Readable kebab-case slug with a kind prefix, e.g. D-control-loop, T-event-store, C-event-log. Self-explaining anywhere it appears. The CLI refuses a slug already in use; two branches choosing the same slug is rare and caught by the id-collision rule. Longer to type.
Decisions raised by a task are numbered within it (D-R1-1); the lead's on main stay D-013. Unique without coordination, but just as opaque as today.
A hidden ULID is the real id; a short number is assigned when the item reaches main. Robust, but an item has no stable readable name until it is merged.

context.summary: The lead found bare ids unreadable, and R1 and R2 both had to invent placeholder ids because no owner hands them out. Existing ids (D-001..D-019, R1, R2, T0..T10, C1..C5) would be migrated by the one-off import (T9), keeping old ids as aliases so links keep working.
